ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r2.claim: The closing passage first depicts the fate of those who accept the true call and then the fate of those who deny it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r2.anchor: the fate of those people is mentioned who will profess faith in this true call; then the fate of those people is depicted

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.claim: Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.anchor: each part of it is deeply related to its central theme

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388/r9.claim: The punishment is never eased or reduced, like a fever that briefly subsides and loses heat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388/r9.anchor: لا يفتر عنهم: أي لا يخفف ولا ينقص، من قولهم: فترت عنه الحمى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p388/r10.claim: Mublis describes someone silent and despairing of any good.

STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r18.claim: An extended contrast of believers’ and disbelievers’ fates in the Hereafter follows these examples.
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r18.anchor: there is an extended contrast of the fate of believers and disbelievers in the Hereafter (vv. 66–78)

NAHHAS:v4p120/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p120/r7.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p120/r7.claim: Al-Farra says Abdullah's reading has fīhā, referring to Hell; the form fīhi refers to the punishment.
NAHHAS:v4p120/r7.anchor: قال الفراء وفي قراءة عبد الله ( وهم فيها ) يريد جهنم ومن قال فيه أراد العذاب

SAMIN-DURR:43:75/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:75/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:75/r1.claim: لا يفتر عنهم is a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:43:75/r1.anchor: قوله: { لا يفتر عنهم }: جملة حالية، وكذلك

SAMIN-DURR:43:75/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:75/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:75/r2.claim: وهم فيه مبلسون is also a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:43:75/r2.anchor: وكذلك { وهم فيه مبلسون }: وقرأ عبد الله

SAMIN-DURR:43:75/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:75/r3.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:43:75/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads فيها, referring to the Fire, indicated by the mention of punishment.
SAMIN-DURR:43:75/r3.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله " وهم فيها " أي: في النار لدلالة العذاب عليها.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p206/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p206/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p206/r7.claim: The closing section first tells believers and disbelievers their respective fates, then assures the Prophet to disregard mockers, and ends by restating tawḥīd and rejecting intercession as a means of rescue.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p206/r7.anchor: first the believers are informed of their good fate and the disbelievers are informed of their evil fate

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p211/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p211/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p211/r5.claim: The all-encompassing torment will never be suspended, diminished, or removed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p211/r5.anchor: it will not be taken away from them even temporarily nor will it be reduced in extent, let alone being salvaged from it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p211/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p211/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p211/r6.claim: They will be entirely without hope, including the far-fetched expectation of relief or release that might console someone in hardship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p211/r6.anchor: they will find themselves with no hope in this torment.

NASHR:v1p215/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p215/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p215/r1.claim: The main source of faulty recitation in the author's region is habitual overemphasis and excessive thickening, acquired without learning from reliable teachers; sound rules are therefore needed.
NASHR:v1p215/r1.anchor: أصل الخلل الوارد على ألسنة القراء في هذه البلاد وما التحق بها هو إطلاق التفخيمات والتغليظات

NASHR:v1p215/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p215/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p215/r2.claim: Strong and weak, emphatic and light letters affect one another in connected speech; accurate pronunciation requires strenuous practice, precision, and training.
NASHR:v1p215/r2.anchor: فيجذب القوي الضعيف ويغلب المفخم المرقق، فيصعب على اللسان النطق بذلك على حقه

NASHR:v1p215/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p215/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p215/r3.claim: All low-tongue letters are light except specified cases of the divine-name lām, some emphatic letters in certain transmissions, and rāʾ; elevated letters are always emphatic.
NASHR:v1p215/r3.anchor: فاعلم أن الحروف المستفلة كلها مرققة لا يجوز تفخيم شيء منها إلا اللام من اسم الله

NASHR:v1p215/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p215/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p215/r4.claim: Alif has no inherent light or emphatic quality: it follows the preceding letter. Earlier warnings about lightening it target exaggerated pronunciation that makes it resemble wāw.
NASHR:v1p215/r4.anchor: وأما الألف فالصحيح أنها لا توصف بترقيق ولا تفخيم، بل بحسب ما يتقدمها

NASHR:v1p215/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p215/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله محمد بن بصخان
NASHR:v1p215/r5.claim: Ibn Baṣkhān's treatise rejects denying the emphatic alif and attributes that denial to ignorance, poor natural disposition, or lack of understanding.
NASHR:v1p215/r5.anchor: ورأيت من ذلك تأليفا للإمام أبي عبد الله محمد بن بصخان سماه:

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#3/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses the damned as surrendered and despairing.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p202#3/r1.anchor: أنا معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ مبلسون ﴾ قال أي مستسلمون

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r1.claim: Their punishment is never eased; the root of ‘futūr’ indicates weakening in any form, as when a fever subsides briefly.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r1.anchor: والمادة بأي صيغة كانت تدل على الضعف مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r2.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r2.claim: Abdullah reads ‘fīhā,’ referring to Hell rather than the punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r2.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله فيها أي في جهنم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r3.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r3.claim: Al-Raghib defines ‘iblās’ as grief from severe distress and says Iblis’s name derives from it, according to one account.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r3.anchor: قال الراغب : الإبلاس الحزن المعترض من شدة البأس

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r4.claim: It is also explained as silence and loss of argument: a despairing person often falls quiet and forgets what to say.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102/r4.anchor: ولما كان المبلس كثيرا ما يلزم السكوت وينسى ما يعنيه قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r3.claim: Their call can coexist with despair as they fall silent at times and cry out at others during prolonged punishment; one objection is that alternating states do not suit the continuous clause ‘they are despairing.’
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r3.anchor: لأنه صراخ وتمني للموت من فرط الشدة وأما على التفسير الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r4.claim: Another reply says the coordinating wāw does not require sequence, so calling need not follow despair; Alusi notes the circumstantial clause remains tied to their abiding state.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p102#3/r4.anchor: وقيل إن نادوا معطوف بالواو وهي لا تقتضي ترتيبا ولا يخفى أن تلك الجملة حالية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r3.claim: Their punishment does not relent, and they are despairing in it; God did not wrong them, for they wronged themselves.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p222/r3.anchor: لا يفتر عنهم وهم فيه مبلسون وما ظلمناهم ولكن كانوا هم الظالمين

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:75-76/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:75-76/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:75-76/r1.claim: The punishment is not eased; the root conveys weakness, as when a fever subsides.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:75-76/r1.anchor: لا يخفف عنهم من فترت عنه الحمى إذا سكنت قليلا

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:75-76/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:75-76/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:75-76/r2.claim: They despair of escape while in the punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:75-76/r2.anchor: في العذاب { مبلسون } آيسون من النجاة

DURR-FULL:v7p394/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses their state in Hell as resigned and subdued.
DURR-FULL:v7p394/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وهم فيه مبلسون}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r2.claim: One function is to complete the warning begun at 43:65 and developed at 43:66–67, whose detail was interrupted by the promise to believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r2.anchor: أحدهما : إتمام التفصيل لما أجمله الوعيد الذي في قوله تعالى : { فويل للذين ظلموا من عذاب يوم أليم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r3.claim: Alternatively, it is a resumptive explanation prompted by the question of what happens to the opposite of the believers just described.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r3.anchor: الموقع الثاني : أنها كالاستئناف البياني يثيره ما يسمع من وصف أحوال المؤمنين المتقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r4.claim: On either account, the sentence has no syntactic position in the larger construction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r4.anchor: والموقعان سواء في كون الجملة لا محل لها من الإعراب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r7.claim: The clause is circumstantial with respect to the Hellfire punishment; yufattaru is the doubled form of fatara, used transitively here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r7.anchor: وجملة { لا يفتر عنهم } في موضع الحال من { عذاب جهنم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r8.claim: The punishment does not let up; no one lessens or calms it for them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p257/r8.anchor: و { يفتر } مضاعف فتر ، إذا سكن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p258/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p258/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p258/r1.claim: The clause about their despair is coordinated with the statement that the criminals remain in Hell’s punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p258/r1.anchor: { وهم فيه مبلسون } عطف على جملة { إن المجرمين في عذاب جهنم خالدون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p258/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p258/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p258/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAshur defines iblās as despair and humiliation; against al-Zamakhshari, he treats silence as an implication, not part of the word’s definition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p258/r2.anchor: وزاد الزمخشري في معنى الإبلاس قيد السكوت ولم يذكره غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r1.claim: After describing the people of Paradise, the passage turns to the disbelievers' lasting punishment in the Fire so the warning is clear.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r1.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى حال أهل الجنة وما يقال لهم، عقب ذلك بذكر حال الكفرة من الخلود في النار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r3.speaker: قتادة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r3.claim: Mublis means cast away and despairing of any good outcome.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r3.anchor: والمبلس: المبعد اليائس من الخيرة، قاله قتادة وغيره.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r4.claim: Ibn Masud reads وهم مبلسون, clarifying that they are in Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p64/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: «وهم مبلسون» أي في جهنم.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#3/r1.claim: The torment is not eased for them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ لا يفتر ﴾ أي لا يخفف ﴿ عنهم وهم فيه ﴾ يعني في العذاب ﴿ مبلسون ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ عنهم وهم فيه ﴾ يعني في العذاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#3/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#3/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba says they are despairing of God's mercy; Ibn al-Jawzi refers to his earlier discussion at al-An'am 44.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p329#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ مبلسون ﴾ قال ابن قتيبة آيسون من رحمة الله وقد شرحنا هذا في الأنعام 44

BURSEVI:v8p302#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p302#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p302#2/r2.claim: La yuftar means their torment is neither eased nor reduced; the verb suggests weakening and slackening.
BURSEVI:v8p302#2/r2.anchor: لا يخفف العذاب عنهم ولا ينقص مقولهم فترت عنه الحمى إذ سكنت قليلا ونقص حرها

BURSEVI:v8p302#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p302#2/r3.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p302#2/r3.claim: Al-Raghib defines fatr as stillness after intensity, softness after severity, weakness after strength.
BURSEVI:v8p302#2/r3.anchor: قال الراغب : الفتر سكون بعد حدة ولين بعد شدة وضعف بعد قوة

BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r1.claim: Mublisun describes despair of escape, rest, or lighter punishment.
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r1.anchor: آيسون من النجاة والراحة وخفة العقوبات

BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r2.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r2.claim: One account says a criminal is shut into a coffin of fire and entombed there eternally, unable to see or be seen.
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r2.anchor: في تابوت من النار ، ثم يردم عليه ، فيبقى فيه خالدا

BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r3.speaker: تاج المصادر
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r3.claim: Taj al-Masadir glosses iblas as despair, brokenness, and sorrow.

BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r4.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r4.claim: Al-Mufradat defines iblas as sorrow from intense despair, relates Iblis's name to it, and says the despairing fall silent after losing their argument.
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r4.anchor: وفي "المفردات" : الإبلاس : الحزن المعترض من شدة اليأس

BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r5.claim: Al-Taʾwilat al-Najmiyya reads an implied contrast: monotheists may enter Hell but do not remain there, and their punishment is eased.
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r5.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : في الآية إشارة إلى أن أهل التوحيد

BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r6.claim: A report says God causes monotheists in Hell to die until they are brought out; the dead feel no pain.
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r6.anchor: وقد ورد في الخبر أنه يميتهم الحق إماتة إلى أن يخرجهم من النار.

BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r7.claim: Despair characterizes unbelievers; believers in affliction retain hope until their sorrows end.
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r7.anchor: وهذه صفة الكفار والمؤمنون ، وإن كانوا في بلائهم

BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r8.speaker: قال بعض الشيوخ
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r8.claim: Some Sufi elders say a believer's ordeal in Hell can ease the heart more than worldly life: here the trial assures eventual rescue, unlike worldly fear of ruin.
BURSEVI:v8p302#3/r8.anchor: وقال بعض الشيوخ : إن حال المؤمن من النار من وجه أروح لقلوبهم من حالهم في الدنيا

MUQATIL:43:74-78/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:74-78/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:74-78/r2.claim: Their punishment does not lessen for even an instant.
MUQATIL:43:74-78/r2.anchor: لا يفتر عنهم } ، العذاب طرفة عين

MUQATIL:43:74-78/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:74-78/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:74-78/r3.claim: They despair of every good, are certain of punishment, receive tidings of evil, have blue eyes and black faces.
MUQATIL:43:74-78/r3.anchor: يعني آيسون من كل خير مستيقنين بكل عذاب، مبشرين بكل سوء، زرق الأعين، سود الوجوه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#3/r1.claim: This is another predicate: the punishment is neither eased nor diminished.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#3/r1.anchor: خبر آخر أي لا يخفف ولا ينقص

NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p120#3/r2.claim: They are despairing of relief and bewildered in the punishment.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:74-76/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:74-76/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:74-76/r3.claim: Mublisun means despairing of mercy; another view says they are silent in despair.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:74-76/r3.anchor: أي آيسون من الرحمة. وقيل: ساكتون سكوت يأس

STUDYQURAN:43:74/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:74/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:43:74/r1.claim: The punishment is not lightened even for a single moment.
STUDYQURAN:43:74/r1.anchor: for a single moment (IK), since it is inescapable (25:65)

STUDYQURAN:43:74/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:74/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:74/r2.claim: Its inescapability means there is no security from the punishment.
STUDYQURAN:43:74/r2.anchor: since it is inescapable (25:65), and there is no security from the punishment (70:28)

STUDYQURAN:43:74/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:74/r3.speaker: Iṣ
STUDYQURAN:43:74/r3.claim: Mublisūn conveys regret and being dumbstruck, unable to speak in one’s own defense.
STUDYQURAN:43:74/r3.anchor: which also connotes regret and the experience of being dumbstruck, unable to speak in defense of oneself (Iṣ)

QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r1.claim: Polytheist unbelievers remain in Hell forever, with neither respite nor reduction; monotheists who enter it do not remain forever.
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r1.anchor: هؤلاء هم الكفار المشركون ، فهم أهل الخلود

QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r2.speaker: خبر صحيح
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r2.claim: A report graded sound says God does not let the people of the Fire die before taking them out, since the dead cannot feel or suffer.
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r2.anchor: ورد في الخبر الصحيح : أنه لا يميتهم الحق - سبحانه - إماتة

QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r3.claim: Iblas means disappointment; this implies believers in Hell are not despairing but remain hopeful until their reckoning ends.
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r3.anchor: الإبلاس من الخيبة ويدل ذلك على أن المؤمنين لا يأس لهم فيها

QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r4.speaker: الشيوخ
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r4.claim: The shaykhs say a believer's state in Hell is in one respect easier than worldly life: he fears destruction today but is certain of rescue tomorrow.
QUSHAYRI:v3p181/r4.anchor: إن حال المؤمن في النار - من وجه - أروح لقلبه من حاله في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v20p648/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r2.claim: Their punishment is not eased or reduced.
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r2.anchor: لا يخفف عنهم العذاب وأصل الفتور: الضعف

TAB-FULL:v20p648/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r3.claim: The root sense of futūr is weakness.

TAB-FULL:v20p648/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r4.claim: The pronoun in fīhi refers to the punishment; the meaning is that they are in Hell, despairing of rescue and submitting to torment.
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r4.anchor: والهاء في فيه من ذكر العذاب

TAB-FULL:v20p648/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r5.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r5.claim: ʿAbd Allāh’s reading has فيها, meaning that they are in Hell, while the received wording has فيه referring to the punishment.
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r5.anchor: في قراءة عبد الله: «وهم فيها مبلسون» والمعنى: وهم في جهنم مبلسون

TAB-FULL:v20p648/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r6.claim: Mublisūn here means hopeless of salvation, despairing, and surrendered to torment and affliction.
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r6.anchor: والمبلس في هذا الموضع: هو الآيس من النجاة الذي قد قنط فاستسلم للعذاب والبلاء

TAB-FULL:v20p648/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r7.claim: Qatāda glosses mublisūn as surrendered to the punishment.

TAB-FULL:v20p648/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r8.claim: In another report Qatāda says they are despairing.
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وهم فيه مبلسون} [الزخرف: 75] قال: «آيسون»

TAB-FULL:v20p648/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r9.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p648/r9.claim: Al-Suddī says their condition has changed.

TABATABAI:43:71-77/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:71-77/r16.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:71-77/r16.claim: Mublisūn are despairing of mercy or escape from the Fire.
TABATABAI:43:71-77/r16.anchor: ويأسهم من الرحمة أو من الخروج من النار

TABRISI:43:72-75/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:72-75/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:72-75/r5.anchor: وهم فيه مبلسون } آيسون من كل خير

FARRA:v3p37/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p37/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p37/r1.claim: The unceasing torment is the punishment they are in.
FARRA:v3p37/r1.anchor: وقوله: لا يفتر عنهم وهم فيه مبلسون (75) فى العذاب.

FARRA:v3p37/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p37/r2.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v3p37/r2.claim: Abdullah reads فيها, referring to Hell; مبلس means despairing of salvation.
FARRA:v3p37/r2.anchor: وفى قراءة عبد الله: (وهم فيها مبلسون) ، ذهب إلى جهنم، والمبلس: القانط اليائس من النجاة .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p400#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p400#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p400#5/r1.claim: Mublisūn means despairing of God's mercy.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p400#5/r1.anchor: وهم فيه مبلسون} أي يائسون من رحمة الله.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:75/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:75/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:75/r1.claim: The torment is not eased for them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:75/r1.anchor: لا يفتر عنهم } أي: لا يخفف عنهم العذاب { وهم فيه مبلسون } ساكتون سكوت يأس.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:75/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:75/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:75/r2.anchor: وهم فيه مبلسون } ساكتون سكوت يأس.

ELMALILI:43:68-89/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r13.claim: The author renders their punishment as never being eased and their condition as having lost all hope.
ELMALILI:43:68-89/r13.anchor: Kendilerinden o azab gevşetilmez ve onlar onun içinde her ümidi kesmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r1.claim: Placing opposites side by side after describing Paradise makes the difference between the two conditions clearer and more vivid.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r1.anchor: Zıtların yan yana getirilmesi ve bu şekilde karşılaştırma yapılması her birinin farkını daha açık ve canlı bir şekilde ortaya çıkarır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r2.claim: God wrongs no one: imposing duties without giving people the ability and means to fulfill them would be unjust, and God has provided both.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r2.anchor: İnsana hem bazı ödevler yüklemek hem de bunları yapacak güç ve imkân vermemek zulümdür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r3.claim: Unbelievers and sinners misuse the means they were given and thereby open the road to Hell themselves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:74/r3.anchor: inkârcı ve günahkâr kullar ellerindeki imkânı kötüye kullanmış, kendilerine cehennemin yolunu yine kendileri açmışlardır

BURHAN:v1p429#2/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p429#2/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p429#2/r4.claim: Sīn in ‘they are dragged’ denotes pulling, whereas ṣād in ‘they are accompanied’ denotes companionship.
BURHAN:v1p429#2/r4.anchor: فبالسين من الجر وبالصاد من الصحبة
